Königstuhl Landeplatz
notes: Easy, but on the far side of the Neckar. There some south of the Neckar, but you don't really want to use these.

name: Tegelberg LP Talstation Tegelbergbahn
notes: Be very precise with landings.  The LZ is very nicely marked and maintained, but they are strict about patterns and careful landings - no hot dogging near the LZ or they will have words for you.

name: Laucha Westhang Landeplatz
notes: no problems if you blunder, landing field is just below and lots of extra areas for inexperienced pilots.

name: Schäfersfeld Landeplatz Bruhansenhof
notes:
Big area, quite a bit far away from takeoff.
From takeoff turn left about 1.5 km away.

name: Ipf Landeplatz
notes: Plain field, keep an eye on the Kables arround the field

name: Loffenau Landewiese
notes: landing spot

name: Kohleckle Landeplatz
notes: South of that motocross circle thing.

name: Osterfelder Landeplatz
notes: Huge grassy field. Watch for strong valley winds, and thermals in the landing zone.

name: Blomberg Landeplatz
notes:
Land only north of the road! Wind comes usually from the east.
Do not park or bring cars here!

name: Jägerberg Landeplatz 2 für GS
notes:
just below takeoff there is a big meadow where you can land and walk up again easily; if you decide to fly down all the way, pick the hugh patch on the other side of the settlement - there is one lonely tree with a windsock, the usual pickup spot for the locals 
if you do land on top, do so close to the takeoff or avoid the rotor just behind and land about 200m further back (in between you might get a nasty whack)

name: Pasel Landeplatz
notes: Landing only on this small gras strip between river and farm land.

big landing area

name: Schäferstuhl Landing

name: Nortmoor Landing
notes: same as start

name: Hochblauen Nord Landing
notes:
The Landing area is near the small village Lipburg. You will need min. 5.5 to reach the landing zone.  
The Landing field is near the cemetery on top of the hill beside. The filed is marked by a windsock.

name: Landing Waldkirch
notes:
Medium due to mixed traffic (PG and HG) near Waldkirch/Heimeck and/or Glottertal. 
Southern takeoff can partly be used for toplanding.

name: Schleppgelände Dischingen Landing
notes:
Landing on east side: Easy to land

Landing on west side: A little special, ask the locals before flight.

name: Blankenhain Landing
notes:
just below takeoff there is a small stretch of grass, just be sure there is nothing laboured. 
In general pilots land on top where you take off. Make sure not to land too far back - there might be some nasty rotors!

name: Katzenkopf Landing
